STEPS: Identify all active x.ai automation processes and workflows.
Catalog triggers, actions, and data dependencies.
Disable or pause existing x.ai automations to avoid conflicts.
Revoke or remove permissions related to old x.ai endpoints.
Backup existing automation data for reference.
Nullify all outdated automation processes to ensure they cannot be reactivated.
Log every nullification attempt with timestamp, outcome, and process ID.
Set up the new system environment and verify compatibility with your existing data sources.
Configure linear memory modules for sequential task execution and feedback loops.
Implement checkpoints to allow for self-correction and historical context tracking.
Connect the new system to current apps, databases, and APIs.
Ensure all event triggers and responses are updated to use the new linear memory pathways.
Run a trial period where the new system operates in parallel without active outputs to verify performance.
After successful testing, fully switch over and monitor tasks for drift or errors.
Regularly review memory logs to fine-tune closed-loop logic.
Schedule periodic updates to ensure compatibility with new tasks or workflow expansions.
